input.quote: The initial term of this Agreement shall be one (1) year from the Effective Date (the "Initial Term"). This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions (together with the Initial Term, such additional periods the "Term"). Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
input.rationale: Section 4(a) sits at the playbook fallback, so we are not redlining it. The committed period is a 1-year Initial Term (not a multi-year commitment), and the detection standard only treats the absence of a convenience right as a deviation where the term exceeds 12 months. Following the Initial Term, AP holds a symmetric convenience right on ninety (90) days' written notice, which is inside the fallback's 60–90 day window. Kubient's own convenience right is not confined to term-end, but it requires 90 days' notice and so does not reach the walk-away threshold of "fewer than 90 days' notice"; the Initial Term lock-out prevents Kubient from exiting mid-term. On the money side, Kubient's entitlement to "all fees generated during the termination period" is effectively limited to the 90-day notice period (approximately three months' fees), consistent with the fallback cap of no more than 3 months' fees, and it applies equally whichever party terminates. Noted but not flagged: we do not get the preferred 30-day notice, and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees — that mechanic is inapplicable here because Section 5 is a revenue-share under which Kubient pays AP rather than AP prepaying fees. Kubient's convenience right not being restricted to the end of a renewal term is likewise a sub-element short of the preferred wording rather than a material failure.
